input: What are the top 5 most frequent customers who have purchased bakery goods?
output: SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, COUNT(r.ReceiptNumber) AS PurchaseFrequency FROM receipts r JOIN customers c ON r.CustomerId = c.Id GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY PurchaseFrequency DESC LIMIT 5;

input: What are the top 3 goods with the highest average sale price?
output: WITH TopGoodsCTE AS (  SELECT g.Id, AVG(g.Price) AS AverageSalePrice  FROM items i  JOIN goods g  ON i.Item = g.Id  GROUP BY g.Id )  SELECT tg.Id, tg.AverageSalePrice  FROM TopGoodsCTE tg  ORDER BY tg.AverageSalePrice DESC  LIMIT 3;

input: What are the top 5 most frequently purchased products in our bakery during the weekends?
output: With WeekendReceipts AS (SELECT r.ReceiptNumber, r.CustomerId FROM receipts r WHERE CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END = 'Weekend') SELECT g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, COUNT(*) AS PurchaseCount FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id JOIN WeekendReceipts wr ON i.Receipt = wr.ReceiptNumber GROUP BY g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor ORDER BY PurchaseCount DESC LIMIT 5;

input: What are the top 5 most revenue-generating products in our bakery?
output: With ProductRevenue AS (SELECT i.Item, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY i.Item) SELECT g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, pr.TotalRevenue AS Revenue FROM ProductRevenue pr JOIN goods g ON pr.Item = g.Id ORDER BY pr.TotalRevenue DESC LIMIT 5;

input: What items have been purchased in our bakery?
output: SELECT DISTINCT g.Id, g.Flavor, g.Food FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id ORDER BY g.Flavor, g.Food;

input: How many times has each item been purchased?
output: SELECT g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, COUNT(*) AS PurchaseCount FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor ORDER BY PurchaseCount DESC;

input: What are the top 5 most frequently purchased items?
output: SELECT g.Id, g.Flavor, COUNT(*) AS PurchaseCount FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Id, g.Flavor ORDER BY PurchaseCount DESC LIMIT 5;

input: Which bakery goods generated the most revenue during weekdays in October 2007?
output: WITH WeekdayTotals AS (SELECT i.Item, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue, g.Food, g.Flavor FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id JOIN receipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber WHERE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) >= 1 AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 31 AND CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) THEN 'Weekday' ELSE 'Weekend' END = 'Weekday' GROUP BY i.Item, g.Food, g.Flavor) SELECT wt.Item, wt.TotalRevenue, wt.Food, wt.Flavor FROM WeekdayTotals wt ORDER BY wt.TotalRevenue DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which customers purchased the most varieties of goods during the early days of October 2007?
output: With CustomerPurchases AS (SELECT c.Id, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Id) AS VarietyCount FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) <= 10 AND SUBSTR(r.Date, 7, 4) = '2007' GROUP BY c.Id) SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, cp.VarietyCount FROM CustomerPurchases cp JOIN customers c ON cp.Id = c.Id ORDER BY cp.VarietyCount DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which customers spent the most in total at our bakery during the first week of October 2007?
output:
WITH CustomerTotals AS (
  SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalSpent
  FROM customers c
  JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId
  JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt
  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id
  WHERE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 7 AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 7, 4) AS INTEGER) = 2007
  GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName
)
SELECT *
FROM CustomerTotals
ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC
LIMIT 10;

input: Which customers spent the most in total at our bakery on weekends during October 2007?
output: With WeekendCustomersCTE AS (  SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalSpent  FROM customers c  JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId  JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id  WHERE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) >= 1 AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 31 AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 5, 4) AS INTEGER) = 2007 AND CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END = 'Weekend'  GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName)  SELECT * FROM WeekendCustomersCTE ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC LIMIT 10;

output: WITH OctoberReceipts AS (SELECT r.ReceiptNumber FROM receipts r WHERE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) = 2007 AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 6, 2) AS INTEGER) = 10) SELECT OctoberReceipts.ReceiptNumber FROM OctoberReceipts;

input: What is the total amount spent on each of these receipts?
output: WITH CustomerTotals AS (  SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, r.ReceiptNumber, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalSpent  FROM customers c  JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId  JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id  WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) = '10' AND SUBSTR(r.Date, 4, 4) = '2007'  GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, r.ReceiptNumber )  SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, c.ReceiptNumber, c.TotalSpent  FROM CustomerTotals c  ORDER BY c.TotalSpent DESC  LIMIT 10;

input: Which customers are associated with these receipts and what is their total spending?
output: WITH CustomerTotals AS (SELECT r.CustomerId, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalSpent FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) = '10' AND SUBSTR(r.Date, 7, 4) = '2007' GROUP BY r.CustomerId) SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, ct.TotalSpent FROM customers c JOIN CustomerTotals ct ON c.Id = ct.CustomerId ORDER BY ct.TotalSpent DESC LIMIT 10;

input: What is the total revenue for each weekend day of the month?
output: With ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT i.Receipt, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY i.Receipt) SELECT CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS DayType, SUM(rt.Total) AS TotalRevenue FROM receipts r JOIN ReceiptTotals rt ON r.ReceiptNumber = rt.Receipt GROUP BY DayType;

input: What is the average transaction value for each day of the last week?
output: WITH ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT i.Receipt, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY i.Receipt), LastWeekReceipts AS (SELECT r.ReceiptNumber, r.Date FROM receipts r WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 8) >= DATE('now', '-7 days')) SELECT CASE CAST(SUBSTR(lwr.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' ELSE 'Sunday' END AS DayOfWeek, AVG(rt.Total) AS AverageTransactionValue FROM LastWeekReceipts lwr JOIN ReceiptTotals rt ON lwr.ReceiptNumber = rt.Receipt GROUP BY DayOfWeek ORDER BY CASE DayOfWeek WHEN 'Monday' THEN 1 WHEN 'Tuesday' THEN 2 WHEN 'Wednesday' THEN 3 WHEN 'Thursday' THEN 4 WHEN 'Friday' THEN 5 WHEN 'Saturday' THEN 6 WHEN 'Sunday' THEN 7 END;

input: What is the average transaction value for each weekday?
output:
SELECT 
  CASE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' ELSE 'Sunday' END AS DayOfWeek,
  AVG(rt.Total) AS AverageTransactionValue
FROM receipts r
JOIN (
  SELECT i.Receipt, SUM(g.Price) AS Total
  FROM items i
  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id
  GROUP BY i.Receipt
) rt ON r.ReceiptNumber = rt.Receipt
WHERE CASE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' ELSE 'Other' END NOT IN ('Saturday', 'Sunday')
GROUP BY DayOfWeek
ORDER BY CASE DayOfWeek WHEN 'Monday' THEN 1 WHEN 'Tuesday' THEN 2 WHEN 'Wednesday' THEN 3 WHEN 'Thursday' THEN 4 WHEN 'Friday' THEN 5 ELSE 6 END;

input: What is the total value of each receipt?
output: WITH ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT i.Receipt, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY i.Receipt) SELECT Total FROM ReceiptTotals;

input: What day of the week did each receipt occur on?
output: WITH ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT i.Receipt, SUM(g.Price) AS ReceiptTotal FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY i.Receipt) SELECT CASE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' ELSE 'Sunday' END AS DayOfWeek, AVG(rt.ReceiptTotal) AS AverageTransactionValue FROM receipts r JOIN ReceiptTotals rt ON r.ReceiptNumber = rt.Receipt GROUP BY CASE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' ELSE 'Sunday' END ORDER BY CASE DayOfWeek WHEN 'Monday' THEN 1 WHEN 'Tuesday' THEN 2 WHEN 'Wednesday' THEN 3 WHEN 'Thursday' THEN 4 WHEN 'Friday' THEN 5 WHEN 'Saturday' THEN 6 WHEN 'Sunday' THEN 7 END;

input: What is the average total value for each day of the week?
output: WITH ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT i.Receipt, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY i.Receipt) SELECT CASE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' ELSE 'Sunday' END AS DayOfWeek, AVG(rt.Total) AS AverageTransactionValue FROM receipts r JOIN ReceiptTotals rt ON r.ReceiptNumber = rt.Receipt GROUP BY CASE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' ELSE 'Sunday' END ORDER BY CASE DayOfWeek WHEN 'Monday' THEN 1 WHEN 'Tuesday' THEN 2 WHEN 'Wednesday' THEN 3 WHEN 'Thursday' THEN 4 WHEN 'Friday' THEN 5 WHEN 'Saturday' THEN 6 WHEN 'Sunday' THEN 7 END;

input: What are the three most popular flavors based on the total number of items sold?
output: WITH FlavorSales AS (  SELECT g.Flavor, COUNT(*) AS TotalItems  FROM items i  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id  GROUP BY g.Flavor )  SELECT Flavor, TotalItems  FROM FlavorSales  ORDER BY TotalItems DESC  LIMIT 3;

input: What are the top three days of the week with the highest average purchase value?
output: WITH DayWisePurchaseValue AS (SELECT CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) AS Day, AVG(g.Price) AS AvgPurchaseValue FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER)) SELECT CASE Day WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' WHEN 7 THEN 'Sunday' END AS DayOfWeek, AvgPurchaseValue FROM DayWisePurchaseValue ORDER BY AvgPurchaseValue DESC LIMIT 3;

input: What are the three most popular product categories based on total sales during the last quarter?
output:
WITH LastQuarterReceipts AS (
  SELECT r.ReceiptNumber, r.Date, r.CustomerId
  FROM receipts r
  WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 5, 2) = '10' OR SUBSTR(r.Date, 5, 2) = '11' OR SUBSTR(r.Date, 5, 2) = '12'
)
SELECT g.Food AS Category, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalSales
FROM items i
JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id
JOIN LastQuarterReceipts lqr ON i.Receipt = lqr.ReceiptNumber
GROUP BY g.Food
ORDER BY TotalSales DESC
LIMIT 3;

input: What are the three product categories with the highest average revenue per sale?
output: WITH CategoryRevenue AS (SELECT g.Food AS Category, SUM(g.Price) AS Revenue, COUNT(*) AS SalesCount FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Food) SELECT Category, AVG(Revenue) / AVG(SalesCount) AS AvgRevenuePerSale FROM CategoryRevenue GROUP BY Category ORDER BY AvgRevenuePerSale DESC LIMIT 3;

output: SELECT g.Food FROM goods g;

input: How many goods are sold per category?
output: WITH CategoryTotals AS (SELECT g.Food, COUNT(*) AS TotalItems FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Food) SELECT *, ROUND(TotalItems / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM items), 2) AS AverageItemsPerCategory FROM CategoryTotals ORDER BY TotalItems DESC;

input: What are the top three categories with the highest sales?
output: SELECT g.Food AS Category, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalSales FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Food ORDER BY TotalSales DESC LIMIT 3;

output:
WITH WeekendGoods AS (

  FROM items i 
  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id

input: What is the average revenue per transaction for receipts from customers with the last name 'Brown'?
output: WITH ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT r.ReceiptNumber, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM receipts r JOIN customers c ON r.CustomerId = c.Id JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id WHERE c.LastName = 'Brown' AND SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 4) = '2007' AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 6, 2) AS INTEGER) = 10 GROUP BY r.ReceiptNumber) SELECT AVG(rt.Total) AS AvgRevenuePerTransaction FROM ReceiptTotals rt;

input: Which products generated the most revenue in the first half of 2007?
output: With RevenueCTE AS (SELECT i.Item, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id JOIN receipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber WHERE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 5, 4) AS INTEGER) = 2007 AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 6 GROUP BY i.Item) SELECT g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, r.TotalRevenue FROM RevenueCTE r JOIN goods g ON r.Item = g.Id ORDER BY r.TotalRevenue DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which products generated the highest average revenue per transaction in October 2007?
output: WITH OctoberReceipts AS (SELECT r.ReceiptNumber, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id JOIN receipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) = '10' AND SUBSTR(r.Date, 7, 4) = '2007' GROUP BY r.ReceiptNumber), ProductTotals AS (SELECT g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, SUM(ort.Total) AS AverageRevenue FROM OctoberReceipts ort JOIN items i ON ort.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor) SELECT pt.Id, pt.Food, pt.Flavor, pt.AverageRevenue FROM ProductTotals pt ORDER BY pt.AverageRevenue DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which receipts were from October 2007?
output: With OctoberReceipts AS (SELECT r.ReceiptNumber FROM receipts r WHERE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) = 2007 AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 6, 2) AS INTEGER) = 10) SELECT g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id JOIN OctoberReceipts oct ON i.Receipt = oct.ReceiptNumber GROUP BY g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC LIMIT 10;

input: What are the items and corresponding prices for these receipts?
output: WITH RevenueLeaders AS (SELECT g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id JOIN receipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) >= '10' AND SUBSTR(r.Date, 7, 4) = '2007' GROUP BY g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor) SELECT rl.Id, rl.Food, rl.Flavor, i.Item, g.Price FROM RevenueLeaders rl JOIN items i ON rl.Id = i.Item JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id ORDER BY rl.TotalRevenue DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which products generated the most revenue from these items?
output: WITH RevenueCTE AS (  SELECT g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue  FROM items i  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id  JOIN receipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber  WHERE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) >= 10 AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) = 2007  GROUP BY g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor)  SELECT RevenueCTE.Id, RevenueCTE.Food, RevenueCTE.Flavor, RevenueCTE.TotalRevenue  FROM RevenueCTE  ORDER BY RevenueCTE.TotalRevenue DESC  LIMIT 10;

input: What are our top 10 most popular goods by quantity sold?
output: WITH GoodsSoldCTE AS (SELECT g.Id, COUNT(*) AS QuantitySold FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Id) SELECT gs.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, gs.QuantitySold FROM GoodsSoldCTE gs JOIN goods g ON gs.Id = g.Id ORDER BY gs.QuantitySold DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which day of the week has the highest average revenue per transaction?
output: WITH RevenuePerTransaction AS (SELECT r.Date, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id JOIN receipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber GROUP BY r.Date), DayOfWeekRevenue AS (SELECT CASE CAST(SUBSTR(rpt.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' WHEN 0 THEN 'Sunday' END AS DayOfWeek, AVG(rpt.Total) AS AvgRevenuePerTransaction FROM RevenuePerTransaction rpt GROUP BY CASE CAST(SUBSTR(rpt.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' WHEN 0 THEN 'Sunday' END) SELECT DayOfWeek, AvgRevenuePerTransaction FROM DayOfWeekRevenue ORDER BY AvgRevenuePerTransaction DESC LIMIT 1;

input: What are our top 10 customers by total revenue spent?
output: With CustomerTotals AS (SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalSpent FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName) SELECT Id, FirstName, LastName, TotalSpent FROM CustomerTotals ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Who are our top 5 customers by number of visits during weekdays?
output: WITH WeekdayCustomers AS (                  SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) AS NumberOfVisits                  FROM customers c                  JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId                  WHERE CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) THEN 'Weekday' ELSE 'Weekend' END = 'Weekday'                  GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName)                  SELECT *                  FROM WeekdayCustomers                  ORDER BY NumberOfVisits DESC                  LIMIT 5;

input: What are the receipts for each customer?
output: WITH CustomerCTE AS (SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) AS NumberOfVisits FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName) SELECT CustomerCTE.Id, CustomerCTE.FirstName, CustomerCTE.LastName, CustomerCTE.NumberOfVisits, r.ReceiptNumber FROM CustomerCTE JOIN receipts r ON CustomerCTE.Id = r.CustomerId WHERE CustomerCTE.NumberOfVisits IN (SELECT NumberOfVisits FROM CustomerCTE ORDER BY NumberOfVisits DESC LIMIT 10) ORDER BY CustomerCTE.NumberOfVisits DESC;

input: How many unique receipts does each customer have?
output: WITH CustomerCTE AS (SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) AS NumberOfVisits, COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) AS UniqueReceipts FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName) SELECT CustomerCTE.FirstName, CustomerCTE.LastName, CustomerCTE.NumberOfVisits, CustomerCTE.UniqueReceipts FROM CustomerCTE ORDER BY CustomerCTE.NumberOfVisits DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Who are the top 10 customers by number of unique receipts?
output: SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) AS NumberOfReceipts FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY NumberOfReceipts DESC LIMIT 10;

input: What is the daily item sales trend throughout October 2007?
output: WITH DailySales AS (SELECT SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS Day, COUNT(*) AS DailySales FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 5, 2) = '10' AND SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 4) = '2007' GROUP BY SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2)) SELECT *, CASE WHEN CAST(Day AS INTEGER) <= 10 THEN 'Early October' WHEN CAST(Day AS INTEGER) <= 20 THEN 'Mid October' ELSE 'Late October' END AS TimePeriod FROM DailySales ORDER BY Day;

input: What is the monthly revenue trend by flavor in 2007?
output: With MonthFlavorRevenue AS (  SELECT SUBSTR(r.Date, 7, 4) AS Year, SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS Month, g.Flavor, SUM(g.Price) AS MonthlyRevenue  FROM receipts r  JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id  WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 7, 4) = '2007'  GROUP BY Year, Month, g.Flavor )  SELECT mfr.Year, mfr.Month, mfr.Flavor, mfr.MonthlyRevenue  FROM MonthFlavorRevenue mfr  ORDER BY mfr.Year, mfr.Month, mfr.Flavor;

input: What is the daily revenue trend throughout the first half of October 2007?
output: WITH DailyRevenue AS (SELECT CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) AS Day, SUM(g.Price) AS DailyRevenue FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 5, 2) = '10' AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 15 GROUP BY CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) ORDER BY CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER)) SELECT * FROM DailyRevenue;

input: What receipts dates fall within October 2007?
output: WITH ReceiptsInOct2007 AS (SELECT r.ReceiptNumber, SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 7) AS DatePrefix FROM receipts r WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 7) = '2007-10') SELECT r.Date, SUM(g.Price) AS DailyRevenue FROM ReceiptsInOct2007 roi JOIN receipts r ON roi.ReceiptNumber = r.ReceiptNumber JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY r.Date ORDER BY r.Date;

input: What are the daily sale dates from these receipts?

input: What is the total revenue for each of these daily sale dates?
output: With DailyRevenue AS (SELECT SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS SaleDay, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 6, 4) = '2007' AND SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) BETWEEN '01' AND '31' GROUP BY SaleDay) SELECT SaleDay, TotalRevenue FROM DailyRevenue ORDER BY SaleDay;

input: Which customers have purchased items across multiple receipts?
output: With CustomerReceipts AS (  SELECT c.Id, COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) AS ReceiptCount  FROM customers c  JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId  JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt  GROUP BY c.Id  HAVING ReceiptCount > 1)  SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, cr.ReceiptCount  FROM CustomerReceipts cr  JOIN customers c ON cr.Id = c.Id  ORDER BY cr.ReceiptCount DESC;

input: Which items appear across multiple customers?
output: WITH ItemCustomers AS (SELECT i.Item, c.Id AS CustomerId FROM items i JOIN receipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber JOIN customers c ON r.CustomerId = c.Id) SELECT Item, COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerId) AS CustomerCount, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT CustomerId) AS CustomerIds FROM ItemCustomers GROUP BY Item HAVING CustomerCount > 1 ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC;

input: Which product flavors appear across multiple product categories between 'Cake' and 'Pudding'?

input: Which product flavors appear across at least three product categories?

input: How many categories do each of these flavors belong to?

input: What is the average revenue per transaction?
output: WITH TransactionTotals AS (SELECT i.Receipt, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY i.Receipt) SELECT AVG(tt.Total) AS AverageRevenuePerTransaction FROM TransactionTotals tt;

input: What is the average number of unique items per customer?
output: With CustomerItemCounts AS (SELECT c.Id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.Item) AS ItemCount FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt GROUP BY c.Id) SELECT AVG(ItemCount) AS AverageUniqueItemsPerCustomer FROM CustomerItemCounts;

input: What is the average number of items purchased per transaction on weekends?
output: WITH ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT i.Receipt, COUNT(*) AS ItemCount FROM items i GROUP BY i.Receipt), WeekendReceipts AS (SELECT r.ReceiptNumber FROM receipts r WHERE CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END = 'Weekend') SELECT AVG(rt.ItemCount) AS AverageItemsPerTransactionOnWeekends FROM ReceiptTotals rt JOIN WeekendReceipts wr ON rt.Receipt = wr.ReceiptNumber;

input: What is the average number of unique items purchased per transaction?
output: WITH TransactionItemCounts AS (SELECT i.Receipt, COUNT(DISTINCT i.Item) AS UniqueItemCount FROM items i GROUP BY i.Receipt) SELECT AVG(tic.UniqueItemCount) AS AverageUniqueItemsPerTransaction FROM TransactionItemCounts tic;

input: What is the total count of items per receipt?
output: WITH ReceiptItemCounts AS (SELECT i.Receipt, COUNT(*) AS ItemCount FROM items i GROUP BY i.Receipt) SELECT COUNT(ItemCount) AS TotalCountOfItemsPerReceipt FROM ReceiptItemCounts;

input: How do we group items by their respective receipts?
output: WITH ReceiptItemCounts AS (SELECT i.Receipt, COUNT(*) AS ItemCount FROM items i GROUP BY i.Receipt) SELECT AVG(ric.ItemCount) AS AverageItemsPerTransaction FROM ReceiptItemCounts ric;

input: What is the average of these item counts per receipt?
output: WITH ReceiptItemCounts AS (SELECT i.Receipt, COUNT(*) AS ItemCount FROM items i GROUP BY i.Receipt) SELECT AVG(ric.ItemCount) AS AverageItemsPerTransaction FROM ReceiptItemCounts ric;

input: Which customers have purchased the most unique flavors of food?
output: With CustomerPurchasesCTE AS (SELECT c.Id, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Flavor) AS UniqueFlavors FROM receipts r JOIN customers c ON r.CustomerId = c.Id JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY c.Id) SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, cp.UniqueFlavors FROM CustomerPurchasesCTE cp JOIN customers c ON cp.Id = c.Id ORDER BY UniqueFlavors DESC LIMIT 10;

input: What are the top 5 most common days of the week for customers to make purchases?
output: WITH DayOfWeekCTE AS (SELECT CASE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' WHEN 0 THEN 'Sunday' END AS DayOfWeek FROM receipts r) SELECT DayOfWeek, COUNT(*) AS PurchaseCount FROM DayOfWeekCTE GROUP BY DayOfWeek ORDER BY PurchaseCount DESC LIMIT 5;

input: Which products are most commonly purchased together during weekdays?
output: With ProductPairs AS (SELECT i1.Item AS Product1, i2.Item AS Product2, i1.Receipt FROM items i1 JOIN items i2 ON i1.Receipt = i2.Receipt AND i1.Item < i2.Item), WeekdayPairs AS (SELECT pp.Product1, pp.Product2 FROM ProductPairs pp JOIN receipts r ON pp.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber WHERE CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) THEN 'Weekday' ELSE 'Weekend' END = 'Weekday') SELECT g1.Food || ' - ' || g1.Flavor AS Product1, g2.Food || ' - ' || g2.Flavor AS Product2, COUNT(*) AS PairCount FROM WeekdayPairs wp JOIN goods g1 ON wp.Product1 = g1.Id JOIN goods g2 ON wp.Product2 = g2.Id GROUP BY Product1, Product2 ORDER BY PairCount DESC LIMIT 10;

input: What are the top 5 product pairs that generate the highest revenue when purchased together?
output: WITH ProductPairs AS (  SELECT i1.Item AS Product1, i2.Item AS Product2, g1.Price AS Price1, g2.Price AS Price2  FROM items i1  JOIN items i2 ON i1.Receipt = i2.Receipt AND i1.Item < i2.Item  JOIN goods g1 ON i1.Item = g1.Id  JOIN goods g2 ON i2.Item = g2.Id  )  SELECT Product1, Product2, SUM(Price1 + Price2) AS Revenue, COUNT(*) AS PairCount  FROM ProductPairs  GROUP BY Product1, Product2  ORDER BY Revenue DESC  LIMIT 5;

input: What are the items purchased together in each receipt?
output: With ReceiptPairs AS ( SELECT i.Receipt, g1.Food || ' - ' || g1.Flavor AS Product1, g2.Food || ' - ' || g2.Flavor AS Product2 FROM items i JOIN items i2 ON i.Receipt = i2.Receipt AND i.Item < i2.Item JOIN goods g1 ON i.Item = g1.Id JOIN goods g2 ON i2.Item = g2.Id ) SELECT rp.Receipt, rp.Product1, rp.Product2 FROM ReceiptPairs rp;

input: How are these items associated with their corresponding goods?
output:
WITH ProductPairs AS 
(
  SELECT i1.Item AS Item1, i2.Item AS Item2
  FROM items i1
  JOIN items i2 ON i1.Receipt = i2.Receipt AND i1.Item < i2.Item
)

SELECT g1.Food || ' - ' || g1.Flavor AS Product1, g2.Food || ' - ' || g2.Flavor AS Product2, COUNT(*) AS PairCount
FROM ProductPairs pp
JOIN goods g1 ON pp.Item1 = g1.Id
JOIN goods g2 ON pp.Item2 = g2.Id
GROUP BY Product1, Product2
ORDER BY PairCount DESC
LIMIT 10;

input: Which product pairs have the highest frequency of co-occurrence?
output: WITH ProductPairs AS (SELECT i1.Item AS Item1, i2.Item AS Item2 FROM items i1 JOIN items i2 ON i1.Receipt = i2.Receipt AND i1.Ordinal < i2.Ordinal) SELECT g1.Food || ' - ' || g1.Flavor AS Product1, g2.Food || ' - ' || g2.Flavor AS Product2, COUNT(*) AS PairCount FROM ProductPairs pp JOIN goods g1 ON pp.Item1 = g1.Id JOIN goods g2 ON pp.Item2 = g2.Id GROUP BY Product1, Product2 ORDER BY PairCount DESC LIMIT 10;

input: What day of the week has the highest average transaction value?
output: WITH ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT r.Date, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY r.Date) SELECT CASE CAST(SUBSTR(rt.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' ELSE 'Sunday' END, AVG(rt.Total) FROM ReceiptTotals rt GROUP BY CASE CAST(SUBSTR(rt.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' ELSE 'Sunday' END ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1;

input: Which flavor of goods has the highest number of transactions on weekends?
output: With WeekendTransactions AS (SELECT i.Item, g.Flavor, CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS DayType  FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id),  WeekendFlavorTransactions AS (SELECT Flavor, COUNT(*) AS TransactionCount  FROM WeekendTransactions  WHERE DayType = 'Weekend'  GROUP BY Flavor)  SELECT Flavor, TransactionCount  FROM WeekendFlavorTransactions  ORDER BY TransactionCount DESC  LIMIT 1;

input: What day of the week has the highest total transaction value?
output:
WITH DayTotals AS (
  SELECT 
    CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 = 1 THEN 'Monday'
    WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 = 2 THEN 'Tuesday'
    WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 = 3 THEN 'Wednesday'
    WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 = 4 THEN 'Thursday'
    WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 = 5 THEN 'Friday'
    WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 = 6 THEN 'Saturday'
    ELSE 'Sunday' END AS DayOfWeek,
    SUM(g.Price) AS TotalValue
  FROM receipts r
  JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt
  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id
  GROUP BY CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 = 1 THEN 'Monday'
    WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 = 2 THEN 'Tuesday'
    WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 = 3 THEN 'Wednesday'
    WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 = 4 THEN 'Thursday'
    WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 = 5 THEN 'Friday'
    WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 = 6 THEN 'Saturday'
    ELSE 'Sunday' END
)
SELECT DayOfWeek, TotalValue
FROM DayTotals
ORDER BY TotalValue DESC
LIMIT 1;

input: What are the different days of the week present in the receipts data?
output: SELECT DISTINCT CASE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 0 THEN 'Sunday' WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' END AS DayOfWeek FROM receipts r;

input: How many transactions occurred on each day of the week?
output: WITH DayTransactions AS (SELECT CASE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' ELSE 'Sunday' END AS DayOfWeek, COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) AS TransactionCount FROM receipts r GROUP BY CASE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' ELSE 'Sunday' END) SELECT * FROM DayTransactions ORDER BY TransactionCount DESC;

input: Which day of the week has the highest number of transactions?
output: WITH DayOfWeekCTE AS (SELECT CASE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' ELSE 'Sunday' END AS DayOfWeek, r.ReceiptNumber FROM receipts r) SELECT DayOfWeekCTE.DayOfWeek, COUNT(DISTINCT DayOfWeekCTE.ReceiptNumber) AS TransactionCount FROM DayOfWeekCTE GROUP BY DayOfWeekCTE.DayOfWeek ORDER BY TransactionCount DESC LIMIT 1;

input: Which items have been purchased by at least one customer from each region?
output: WITH ItemRegions AS (SELECT DISTINCT i.Item, c.LastName AS Region FROM items i JOIN receipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber JOIN customers c ON r.CustomerId = c.Id), RegionCount AS (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT LastName) AS TotalRegions FROM customers) SELECT ir.Item, COUNT(DISTINCT ir.Region) AS RegionsPurchased FROM ItemRegions ir GROUP BY ir.Item HAVING RegionsPurchased = (SELECT TotalRegions FROM RegionCount) ORDER BY ir.Item;

input: Which goods have been sold to customers who have purchased from all food categories?
output: With AllCategoryCustomers AS (WITH CustomerCategories AS (SELECT DISTINCT r.CustomerId, g.Food AS Category FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id), CategoryCount AS (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT Food) AS TotalCategories FROM goods) SELECT c.Id, COUNT(DISTINCT cc.Category) AS CategoriesPurchased FROM customers c JOIN CustomerCategories cc ON c.Id = cc.CustomerId CROSS JOIN CategoryCount cat GROUP BY c.Id HAVING CategoriesPurchased = cat.TotalCategories), SoldGoods AS (SELECT g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id JOIN receipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber JOIN AllCategoryCustomers acc ON r.CustomerId = acc.Id) SELECT sg.Id, sg.Food, sg.Flavor FROM SoldGoods sg GROUP BY sg.Id, sg.Food, sg.Flavor;

input: Which customers have purchased at least one item from each product category in the last month?
output: WITH LastMonthReceipts AS (SELECT r.CustomerId FROM receipts r WHERE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 7, 4) AS INTEGER) = CAST(SUBSTR(DATE('now', '-1 month'), 7, 4) AS INTEGER) AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) >= CAST(SUBSTR(DATE('now', '-1 month'), 1, 2) AS INTEGER)), CustomerCategories AS (SELECT DISTINCT r.CustomerId, g.Food AS Category FROM LastMonthReceipts r JOIN items i ON r.CustomerId = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id), CategoryCount AS (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT Food) AS TotalCategories FROM goods) SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS CustomerName, COUNT(DISTINCT cc.Category) AS CategoriesPurchased FROM customers c JOIN CustomerCategories cc ON c.Id = cc.CustomerId CROSS JOIN CategoryCount cat GROUP BY c.Id, CustomerName HAVING CategoriesPurchased = cat.TotalCategories ORDER BY c.Id;

input: Which customers have made the most purchases across all product categories?
output: WITH PurchasesPerCustomer AS (SELECT c.Id, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Food) AS CategoryCount FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY c.Id), MaxPurchases AS (SELECT MAX(CategoryCount) AS MaxPurchaseCount FROM PurchasesPerCustomer) SELECT p.Id, p.CategoryCount FROM PurchasesPerCustomer p JOIN MaxPurchases m ON p.CategoryCount = m.MaxPurchaseCount ORDER BY p.Id;

input: What are the distinct product categories available in the goods table?
output: SELECT DISTINCT g.Food AS Category FROM goods g;

input: For each customer, what are the distinct product categories they have purchased?
output: With CustomerCategories AS (SELECT r.CustomerId, g.Food AS Category FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id) SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS CustomerName, array_agg(DISTINCT Category) AS PurchasedCategories FROM customers c JOIN CustomerCategories cc ON c.Id = cc.CustomerId GROUP BY c.Id, CustomerName ORDER BY c.Id;

input: What is the product variety distribution by customer?
output: WITH CustomerGoods AS (SELECT c.Id, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Id) AS ProductIdCount, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Food) AS FoodCount, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Flavor) AS FlavorCount FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY c.Id) SELECT cg.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, cg.ProductIdCount, cg.FoodCount, cg.FlavorCount FROM CustomerGoods cg JOIN customers c ON cg.Id = c.Id ORDER BY cg.ProductIdCount DESC;

input: What is the revenue distribution by day of the week?
output: WITH RevenueByDay AS (SELECT CASE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' WHEN 0 THEN 'Sunday' END AS DayOfWeek, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY CASE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' WHEN 0 THEN 'Sunday' END) SELECT DayOfWeek, TotalRevenue, ROUND(TotalRevenue * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(g.Price) FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id), 2) AS PercentOfTotalRevenue FROM RevenueByDay ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC;

input: What is the revenue distribution by product category in the last quarter?
output: WITH LastQuarterReceipts AS (SELECT r.ReceiptNumber, i.Item, g.Food, g.Price, r.Date FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id WHERE (CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 5, 2) AS INTEGER) = 10 OR CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 5, 2) AS INTEGER) = 11 OR CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 5, 2) AS INTEGER) = 12) OR (CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 5, 2) AS INTEGER) = 1 AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) = CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) - 1)) SELECT lqr.Food AS Category, SUM(lqr.Price) AS TotalRevenue, ROUND(SUM(lqr.Price) * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(lqr.Price) FROM LastQuarterReceipts), 2) AS PercentOfTotalRevenue FROM LastQuarterReceipts lqr GROUP BY lqr.Food ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC;

input: What is the average revenue per category among receipts with over 5 items?
output: WITH ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT i.Receipt, SUM(g.Price) AS Total, COUNT(*) AS ItemCount FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY i.Receipt), ReceiptTotalsFiltered AS (SELECT * FROM ReceiptTotals WHERE ItemCount > 5) SELECT g.Food AS Category, AVG(rt.Total) AS AverageRevenuePerCategory FROM ReceiptTotalsFiltered rt JOIN items i ON rt.Receipt = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Food ORDER BY AverageRevenuePerCategory DESC;

input: What are the different product categories in the goods table?
output:
SELECT DISTINCT g.Food AS Category
FROM goods g;

input: What is the total revenue for each product category?
output: SELECT g.Food AS Category, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Food ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC;

input: How does the revenue for each product category contribute to the total revenue?
output: WITH TotalRevenueCTE AS (SELECT SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id) SELECT g.Food AS Category, SUM(g.Price) AS CategoryRevenue, ROUND(SUM(g.Price) * 100.0 / tr.TotalRevenue, 2) AS PercentOfTotalRevenue FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id, TotalRevenueCTE tr GROUP BY g.Food ORDER BY CategoryRevenue DESC;

input: Which goods have been sold on more than one weekend day in October 2007?
output: WITH Weekends AS (SELECT r.Date, i.Item FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt WHERE CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END = 'Weekend' AND SUBSTR(r.Date, 5, 4) = '2007' AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 31 AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) >= 1) SELECT g.Id, g.Flavor, g.Food, COUNT(DISTINCT w.Date) AS WeekendCount FROM Weekends w JOIN goods g ON w.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Id, g.Flavor, g.Food HAVING WeekendCount > 1 ORDER BY WeekendCount DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which customers have made purchases of more than one distinct flavor of goods in October 2007?
output: WITH FlavorCTE AS (SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Flavor) AS FlavorCount FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id WHERE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 7) AS TEXT) = '2007-10' GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName) SELECT Id, FirstName, LastName, FlavorCount FROM FlavorCTE WHERE FlavorCount > 1 ORDER BY FlavorCount DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which customers made multiple visits to our bakery in the last quarter of 2007?
output: With CustomerCTE AS (SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 7, 4) = '2007' AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) >= 10) SELECT CustomerCTE.Id, CustomerCTE.FirstName, CustomerCTE.LastName, COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) AS VisitCount FROM CustomerCTE JOIN receipts r ON CustomerCTE.Id = r.CustomerId GROUP BY CustomerCTE.Id, CustomerCTE.FirstName, CustomerCTE.LastName HAVING VisitCount > 1 ORDER BY VisitCount DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which customers made multiple visits to our bakery on weekends in October 2007?
output: With OctoberWeekendReceipts AS (SELECT r.CustomerId FROM receipts r WHERE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) >= 1 AND CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 31 AND CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END = 'Weekend') SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, COUNT(DISTINCT owr.CustomerId) AS WeekendVisitCount FROM customers c JOIN OctoberWeekendReceipts owr ON c.Id = owr.CustomerId GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName HAVING WeekendVisitCount > 1 ORDER BY WeekendVisitCount DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which customers made visits to our bakery in October 2007?
output: SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 7) = '2007-10';

input: How many receipts do each of these customers have?
output: WITH CustomerCTE AS (SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) AS VisitCount FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 7) = '2007-10' GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName HAVING VisitCount > 1) SELECT CustomerCTE.Id, CustomerCTE.FirstName, CustomerCTE.LastName, (SELECT COUNT(r.ReceiptNumber) FROM receipts r WHERE r.CustomerId = CustomerCTE.Id AND SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 7) = '2007-10') AS ReceiptCount FROM CustomerCTE ORDER BY VisitCount DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which customers have more than one receipt among these?
output: WITH CustomerReceipts AS (SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) AS VisitCount FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) = '10' AND SUBSTR(r.Date, 7, 4) = '2007' GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName) SELECT cr.Id, cr.FirstName, cr.LastName, cr.VisitCount FROM CustomerReceipts cr WHERE cr.VisitCount > 1 ORDER BY cr.VisitCount DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which customers have the highest average transaction value?
output: WITH ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT r.CustomerId, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY r.CustomerId), AverageTransactionValue AS (SELECT rt.CustomerId, AVG(rt.Total) AS AvgTransactionValue FROM ReceiptTotals rt GROUP BY rt.CustomerId) SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, atv.AvgTransactionValue FROM AverageTransactionValue atv JOIN customers c ON atv.CustomerId = c.Id ORDER BY atv.AvgTransactionValue DESC LIMIT 10;

input: What are the top 10 most popular food items by sales count?
output: WITH FoodSales AS (  SELECT g.Food, COUNT(*) AS SalesCount  FROM items i  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id  GROUP BY g.Food)  SELECT fs.Food, fs.SalesCount  FROM FoodSales fs  ORDER BY fs.SalesCount DESC  LIMIT 10;

input: Which food products have the highest price to sales ratio in the last three months?
output:
WITH RecentReceipts AS (SELECT r.ReceiptNumber, r.Date, r.CustomerId FROM receipts r WHERE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 7, 4) AS INTEGER) * 100 + CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) >= (CAST(SUBSTR(DATE('now'), 7, 4) AS INTEGER) * 100 + CAST(SUBSTR(DATE('now'), 1, 2) AS INTEGER)) - 3 * 100), 
ProductSales AS (SELECT g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, g.Price, COUNT(*) AS SalesCount, ROUND(g.Price / COUNT(*), 2) AS PriceToSalesRatio 
FROM items i 
JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id 
JOIN RecentReceipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber 
WHERE g.Food IS NOT NULL 
GROUP BY g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, g.Price) 
SELECT * FROM ProductSales ORDER BY PriceToSalesRatio DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which flavors of products have the highest average price to sales ratio?
output: WITH ProductRatios AS (SELECT g.Flavor, ROUND(AVG(g.Price) / AVG(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY g.Flavor), 2) AS AvgPriceToSalesRatio FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Flavor) SELECT * FROM ProductRatios ORDER BY AvgPriceToSalesRatio DESC LIMIT 10;

input: What goods have the highest sales count?
output: SELECT g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, COUNT(*) AS SalesCount FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor ORDER BY SalesCount DESC LIMIT 10;

input: What is the total revenue for each good?
output: WITH GoodSales AS (SELECT g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, g.Price, COUNT(*) AS SalesCount, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, g.Price) SELECT * FROM GoodSales ORDER BY TotalRevenue LIMIT 10;

input: What is the price to sales ratio for each good?
output: With GoodsRatio AS (SELECT g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, g.Price, COUNT(i.Receipt) AS SalesCount, ROUND(g.Price / COUNT(i.Receipt), 2) AS PriceToSalesRatio FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Id, g.Food, g.Flavor, g.Price) SELECT gr.Id, gr.Food, gr.Flavor, gr.Price, gr.SalesCount, gr.PriceToSalesRatio FROM GoodsRatio gr ORDER BY gr.PriceToSalesRatio DESC LIMIT 10;

input: What is the average number of items purchased per receipt for each customer?
output: WITH ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT r.CustomerId, COUNT(i.Item) AS ItemsPerReceipt, r.ReceiptNumber FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt GROUP BY r.CustomerId, r.ReceiptNumber) SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, AVG(r.ItemsPerReceipt) AS AverageItemsPerReceipt FROM ReceiptTotals r JOIN customers c ON r.CustomerId = c.Id GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY AverageItemsPerReceipt DESC;

input: What is the total revenue generated by each type of food?
output: WITH RevenueByFood AS (SELECT g.Food, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Food) SELECT Food, TotalRevenue FROM RevenueByFood ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC;

input: What is the average spending per visit for each customer who has made a purchase in the last 3 months?
output: WITH RecentReceipts AS (SELECT r.CustomerId FROM receipts r WHERE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) >= CAST(SUBSTR(DATE('now'), 1, 2) AS INTEGER) - 3) SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) AS VisitCount, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalSpent, ROUND(SUM(g.Price) / COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber), 2) AS AverageSpendPerVisit FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id WHERE c.Id IN (SELECT CustomerId FROM RecentReceipts) GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY AverageSpendPerVisit DESC;

input: What is the total number of visits for each customer?
output: WITH CustomerVisits AS (SELECT c.Id, COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) AS VisitCount FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId GROUP BY c.Id) SELECT cv.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, cv.VisitCount FROM CustomerVisits cv JOIN customers c ON cv.Id = c.Id ORDER BY cv.VisitCount DESC;

input: What is the total amount spent by each customer?
output: SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalSpent FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC;

input: How do we calculate the average spending per visit for each customer using the total amount spent and number of visits?
output: WITH CustomerTotals AS (SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) AS VisitCount, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalSpent FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName) SELECT Id, FirstName, LastName, VisitCount, TotalSpent, ROUND(TotalSpent / VisitCount, 2) AS AverageSpendPerVisit FROM CustomerTotals ORDER BY AverageSpendPerVisit DESC;

input: How do sales to first-time customers compare to sales to repeat customers in terms of volume and revenue?
output: WITH CustomerCTE AS (SELECT c.Id, r.ReceiptNumber, COUNT(r.ReceiptNumber) OVER (PARTITION BY c.Id) AS ReceiptCount, g.Price FROM receipts r JOIN customers c ON r.CustomerId = c.Id JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id) SELECT CASE WHEN ReceiptCount = 1 THEN 'First-Time' ELSE 'Repeat' END AS CustomerType, COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) AS TransactionCount, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue, COUNT(*) AS ItemsSold, ROUND(SUM(g.Price) / COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber), 2) AS AverageTransactionValue FROM CustomerCTE c JOIN receipts r ON c.ReceiptNumber = r.ReceiptNumber JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY CustomerType;

input: What is the revenue and transaction volume difference between receipts with a single item versus receipts with multiple items?
output: WITH SingleItemReceipts AS (SELECT r.ReceiptNumber, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY r.ReceiptNumber HAVING COUNT(i.Item) = 1), MultiItemReceipts AS (SELECT r.ReceiptNumber, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY r.ReceiptNumber HAVING COUNT(i.Item) > 1) SELECT 'Single Item' AS ReceiptType, COUNT(sir.ReceiptNumber) AS TransactionCount, SUM(sir.TotalRevenue) AS TotalRevenue FROM SingleItemReceipts sir UNION ALL SELECT 'Multi Item' AS ReceiptType, COUNT(mir.ReceiptNumber) AS TransactionCount, SUM(mir.TotalRevenue) AS TotalRevenue FROM MultiItemReceipts mir;

input: How do sales during the first half of the month compare to sales during the second half of the month in terms of volume and revenue?
output:
WITH SalePeriod AS (
SELECT CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 15 THEN 'FirstHalf' ELSE 'SecondHalf' END AS Period,
       COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) AS TransactionCount,
       SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue,
       COUNT(*) AS ItemsSold,
       ROUND(SUM(g.Price) / COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber), 2) AS AverageTransactionValue
FROM receipts r
JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt
JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id
GROUP BY Period)

SELECT *
FROM SalePeriod;

input: How do weekday sales in October compare to weekend sales in October in terms of volume and revenue?
output: With DayTypeCTE AS (  SELECT      CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS DayType,      CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 10 THEN 'Early October' ELSE 'Not October' END AS TimePeriod,      r.ReceiptNumber,      g.Price  FROM receipts r  JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id  WHERE r.Date LIKE '2022-10%' ),  OctoberDayTypeCTE AS (  SELECT      *  FROM DayTypeCTE  WHERE TimePeriod = 'Early October' )  SELECT      d.DayType,      COUNT(DISTINCT d.ReceiptNumber) AS TransactionCount,      SUM(d.Price) AS TotalRevenue,      COUNT(*) AS ItemsSold,      ROUND(SUM(d.Price) / COUNT(DISTINCT d.ReceiptNumber), 2) AS AverageTransactionValue  FROM OctoberDayTypeCTE d  GROUP BY d.DayType;

input: What is the total number of transactions on weekdays and weekends?
output: WITH DayTypeCTE AS (SELECT r.ReceiptNumber, CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS DayType FROM receipts r) SELECT d.DayType, COUNT(d.ReceiptNumber) AS TransactionCount FROM DayTypeCTE d GROUP BY d.DayType;

input: What is the total revenue for weekdays and weekends?
output: WITH DayTypeCTE AS (SELECT r.ReceiptNumber, CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS DayType, g.Price FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id) SELECT DayTypeCTE.DayType, ROUND(SUM(DayTypeCTE.Price), 2) AS TotalRevenue FROM DayTypeCTE GROUP BY DayTypeCTE.DayType ORDER BY DayTypeCTE.DayType;

input: What is the average transaction value for weekdays and weekends?
output: WITH ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT i.Receipt, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id JOIN receipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber GROUP BY i.Receipt) SELECT CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN AVG(rt.Total) ELSE NULL END AS Weekend_Avg, CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 NOT IN (0, 6) THEN AVG(rt.Total) ELSE NULL END AS Weekday_Avg FROM ReceiptTotals rt JOIN receipts r ON rt.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber GROUP BY CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END;

input: Which product category contributes the most to revenue across all flavors?
output: WITH RevenueByFood AS (SELECT g.Food, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Food) SELECT Food, TotalRevenue FROM RevenueByFood ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC LIMIT 1;

input: What is the most common food type purchased by customers?
output: SELECT g.Food, COUNT(*) AS PurchaseCount FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Food ORDER BY PurchaseCount DESC LIMIT 1;

input: What flavor is the most popular among customers who only purchase items from the bakery category?
output:
WITH BakeryGoodsCTE AS (SELECT 'Bakery' AS Category, g.Id, g.Flavor, g.Food, g.Price FROM goods g WHERE g.Food = 'Bakery'),
            BakeryCustomersCTE AS (SELECT i.Receipt, i.Item, r.CustomerId FROM items i JOIN receipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber JOIN BakeryGoodsCTE bg ON i.Item = bg.Id),
            PopularBakeryFlavorsCTE AS (SELECT bg.Flavor, COUNT(*) AS PurchaseCount FROM BakeryCustomersCTE bc JOIN BakeryGoodsCTE bg ON bc.Item = bg.Id GROUP BY bg.Flavor)
            SELECT PopularBakeryFlavorsCTE.Flavor, PopularBakeryFlavorsCTE.PurchaseCount FROM PopularBakeryFlavorsCTE ORDER BY PopularBakeryFlavorsCTE.PurchaseCount DESC LIMIT 1;

input: What flavor is the most popular among customers who made a purchase during the weekend?
output: WITH WeekendCustomers AS (SELECT r.CustomerId FROM receipts r WHERE CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END = 'Weekend') SELECT g.Flavor, COUNT(*) AS PurchaseCount FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id JOIN receipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber JOIN WeekendCustomers wc ON r.CustomerId = wc.CustomerId GROUP BY g.Flavor ORDER BY PurchaseCount DESC LIMIT 1;

input: What are all the unique flavors of goods?
output: SELECT DISTINCT g.Flavor FROM goods g;

input: How many items of each flavor are sold?
output: SELECT g.Flavor, COUNT(*) AS PurchaseCount FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Flavor ORDER BY PurchaseCount DESC;

input: Which flavor has the highest count of items sold?
output: With GoodsSold AS (SELECT g.Flavor, COUNT(*) as Count FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id JOIN receipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber GROUP BY g.Flavor) SELECT Flavor, Count FROM GoodsSold ORDER BY Count DESC LIMIT 1;

input: What flavor of goods has the highest revenue?
output: WITH GoodsRevenue AS (SELECT g.Flavor, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Flavor) SELECT Flavor, TotalRevenue FROM GoodsRevenue ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC LIMIT 1;

input: Which day of the week has the most items sold?
output: WITH DailySales AS (SELECT CASE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' ELSE 'Sunday' END AS DayOfWeek, COUNT(*) AS ItemsSold FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY DayOfWeek) SELECT * FROM DailySales ORDER BY ItemsSold DESC LIMIT 1;

input: What time of the quarter (early, mid, late) has the highest sales?
output: With QuarterlySales AS (SELECT CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 5, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 10 THEN 'Early Quarter' WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 5, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 20 THEN 'Mid Quarter' ELSE 'Late Quarter' END AS TimePeriod, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY TimePeriod) SELECT * FROM QuarterlySales ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC LIMIT 1;

input: What day of the week has the highest sales for October?
output: With ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT r.Date, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY r.Date) SELECT CASE CAST(SUBSTR(rt.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' WHEN 3 THEN 'Wednesday' WHEN 4 THEN 'Thursday' WHEN 5 THEN 'Friday' WHEN 6 THEN 'Saturday' ELSE 'Sunday' END AS DayOfWeek, SUM(rt.TotalRevenue) AS TotalRevenue FROM ReceiptTotals rt WHERE SUBSTR(rt.Date, 1, 4) = '2022' AND SUBSTR(rt.Date, 5, 2) = '10' GROUP BY DayOfWeek ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC LIMIT 1;

input: What is the distribution of receipts across different time periods in October?
output: WITH ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT r.ReceiptNumber, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY r.ReceiptNumber) SELECT CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 10 THEN 'Early October' WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 20 THEN 'Mid October' ELSE 'Late October' END AS TimePeriod, COUNT(r.ReceiptNumber) AS ReceiptCount, SUM(rt.Total) AS TotalRevenue FROM receipts r JOIN ReceiptTotals rt ON r.ReceiptNumber = rt.ReceiptNumber GROUP BY TimePeriod ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC;

input: What is the total revenue generated by each time period?
output:
SELECT
  CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 10 THEN 'Early October'
       WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 20 THEN 'Mid October'

input: Which time period has the highest total revenue?
output: WITH ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT r.Date, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY r.Date) SELECT CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(rt.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 10 THEN 'Early October' WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(rt.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 20 THEN 'Mid October' ELSE 'Late October' END AS TimePeriod, SUM(rt.TotalRevenue) AS TotalRevenue FROM ReceiptTotals rt GROUP BY TimePeriod ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC LIMIT 1;

input: Which products have the most varied flavors?
output: SELECT g.Food, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Flavor) AS UniqueFlavors FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Food ORDER BY UniqueFlavors DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which receipt dates have the most varied customer ages?
output: WITH CustomerAges AS (SELECT r.Date, c.Id, (2023 - SUBSTR(c.LastName, 1, 4)) AS Age FROM receipts r JOIN customers c ON r.CustomerId = c.Id) SELECT ca.Date, COUNT(DISTINCT ca.Age) AS UniqueAges FROM CustomerAges ca GROUP BY ca.Date ORDER BY UniqueAges DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which customers purchase the most varied products during the last quarter?
output: WITH CustomerReceipts AS (SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, r.ReceiptNumber, r.Date FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId WHERE SUBSTR(r.Date, 5, 2) IN ('07', '08', '09')) SELECT cr.Id, cr.FirstName, cr.LastName, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Id) AS UniqueProducts, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Food) AS UniqueCategories, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Flavor) AS UniqueFlavors FROM CustomerReceipts cr JOIN items i ON cr.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY cr.Id, cr.FirstName, cr.LastName ORDER BY UniqueProducts DESC, UniqueCategories DESC, UniqueFlavors DESC LIMIT 10;

input: Which customers purchase the most varied products in the food category, having at least 3 receipts?
output:
WITH VariedCustomers AS (
    SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Food) AS UniqueFoods, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Flavor) AS UniqueFlavors
    FROM customers c
    JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId
    JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt
    JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id AND g.Food = 'Food'
    GROUP BY c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT r.ReceiptNumber) >= 3
)
SELECT *
FROM VariedCustomers
ORDER BY UniqueFoods DESC, UniqueFlavors DESC
LIMIT 10;

input: What goods are purchased by each customer?
output: WITH CustomerGoods AS (SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, g.Id AS GoodsId, g.Food, g.Flavor FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id) SELECT cg.Id, cg.FirstName, cg.LastName, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT cg.Food, ', ') AS Food, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT cg.Flavor, ', ') AS Flavor FROM CustomerGoods cg GROUP BY cg.Id, cg.FirstName, cg.LastName ORDER BY cg.Id;

input: What is the product variety for each customer?
output: WITH CustomerProductVariety AS (SELECT c.Id, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Id) AS UniqueProducts, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Food) AS UniqueCategories, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Flavor) AS UniqueFlavors FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY c.Id) SELECT c.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, CPV.UniqueProducts, CPV.UniqueCategories, CPV.UniqueFlavors FROM customers c JOIN CustomerProductVariety CPV ON c.Id = CPV.Id ORDER BY CPV.UniqueProducts DESC, CPV.UniqueCategories DESC, CPV.UniqueFlavors DESC;

input: Which customers have the highest total product variety?
output: With CustomerVarietyCTE AS (SELECT c.Id, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Id) AS UniqueProducts, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Food) AS UniqueCategories, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Flavor) AS UniqueFlavors FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY c.Id) SELECT CustomerVarietyCTE.Id, c.FirstName, c.LastName, CustomerVarietyCTE.UniqueProducts, CustomerVarietyCTE.UniqueCategories, CustomerVarietyCTE.UniqueFlavors FROM CustomerVarietyCTE JOIN customers c ON CustomerVarietyCTE.Id = c.Id ORDER BY CustomerVarietyCTE.UniqueProducts + CustomerVarietyCTE.UniqueCategories + CustomerVarietyCTE.UniqueFlavors DESC LIMIT 10;

input: What is the average revenue generated by sweet bakery goods on weekends, and how does it compare to weekdays?
output:
WITH WeekendSweetBakery AS (
  SELECT r.Date, SUM(g.Price) AS Total
  FROM receipts r
  JOIN customers c ON r.CustomerId = c.Id
  JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt
  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id
  WHERE g.Food = 'Bakery' AND g.Flavor = 'Sweet' AND CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END = 'Weekend'
  GROUP BY r.Date
),
WeekdaySweetBakery AS (
  SELECT r.Date, SUM(g.Price) AS Total
  FROM receipts r
  JOIN customers c ON r.CustomerId = c.Id
  JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt
  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id
  WHERE g.Food = 'Bakery' AND g.Flavor = 'Sweet' AND CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END = 'Weekday'
  GROUP BY r.Date
)
SELECT 'Weekend' AS DayType, AVG(WeekendSweetBakery.Total) AS AverageRevenue
FROM WeekendSweetBakery
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Weekday' AS DayType, AVG(WeekdaySweetBakery.Total) AS AverageRevenue
FROM WeekdaySweetBakery;

input: What are the top 3 flavor preferences for bakery goods, and what is the total revenue generated by each?
output:
WITH FlavorRevenue AS (
  SELECT g.Flavor, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue
  FROM items i
  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id
  JOIN receipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber
  WHERE g.Food = 'Bakery'
  GROUP BY g.Flavor
)
SELECT Flavor, TotalRevenue
FROM FlavorRevenue
ORDER BY TotalRevenue DESC

input: What is the sales analytics of bakery goods, including the total items sold, revenue generated, and average revenue per item?
output: WITH BakeryAnalytics AS (SELECT g.Food, COUNT(*) AS TotalItems, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Food) SELECT *, AVG(TotalRevenue / TotalItems) OVER () AS AverageRevenuePerItem FROM BakeryAnalytics;

input: What is the distribution of items purchased by customers, and how does it vary by flavor preferences?
output: With CustomerPurchases AS (SELECT c.Id, g.Flavor, COUNT(*) AS PurchaseCount FROM customers c JOIN receipts r ON c.Id = r.CustomerId JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY c.Id, g.Flavor), FlavorCounts AS (SELECT Flavor, COUNT(*) AS Count, SUM(PurchaseCount) OVER (PARTITION BY Flavor) AS Total FROM CustomerPurchases GROUP BY Flavor) SELECT Flavor, Count, Total, CAST(Count AS REAL) / Total AS PurchasePercentage FROM FlavorCounts ORDER BY PurchasePercentage DESC LIMIT 10;

input: What is the product variety index for bakery goods, and how does it impact revenue generation?
output: With BakeryGoods AS (  SELECT g.Food, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Id) AS ProductCount, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Food) AS ProductVariety, COUNT(DISTINCT g.Flavor) AS FlavorVariety  FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id  WHERE g.Food = 'Bakery'  GROUP BY g.Food  ), RevenueImpact AS (  SELECT g.Food, SUM(g.Price) AS TotalRevenue, AVG(g.Price) AS AveragePrice  FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id  WHERE g.Food = 'Bakery'  GROUP BY g.Food  )  SELECT bg.ProductVariety / bg.ProductCount AS ProductVarietyIndex, ri.TotalRevenue, ri.AveragePrice  FROM BakeryGoods bg JOIN RevenueImpact ri ON bg.Food = ri.Food;

input: What are the sales analytics of bakery goods by time period, including total items sold, revenue generated, and average revenue per item, and how do they vary by flavor preferences?
output:
WITH TimePeriodCTE AS ( 
  SELECT i.Item, g.Food, g.Flavor, r.Date, g.Price, 
  CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 10 THEN 'Early October' 
       WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 20 THEN 'Mid October' 
       ELSE 'Late October' END AS TimePeriod 
  FROM items i 
  JOIN receipts r ON i.Receipt = r.ReceiptNumber 
  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id ), 
  
  SalesAnalyticsCTE AS ( 
  SELECT TimePeriod, Food, Flavor, COUNT(*) AS TotalItems, SUM(Price) AS TotalRevenue, 
  SUM(Price) / COUNT(*) AS AverageRevenuePerItem 
  FROM TimePeriodCTE 
  GROUP BY TimePeriod, Food, Flavor ) 
  
  SELECT TimePeriod, Food, Flavor, TotalItems, TotalRevenue, AverageRevenuePerItem 
  FROM SalesAnalyticsCTE 
  ORDER BY TimePeriod, Food, Flavor;

input: What is the average spending pattern of customers during weekdays vs weekends?
output: With WeekdayCTE AS (SELECT r.CustomerId, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id WHERE CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) THEN 'Weekday' ELSE 'Weekend' END = 'Weekday' GROUP BY r.CustomerId), WeekendCTE AS (SELECT r.CustomerId, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id WHERE CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) THEN 'Weekday' ELSE 'Weekend' END = 'Weekend' GROUP BY r.CustomerId) SELECT 'Weekday' AS Period, AVG(WeekdayCTE.Total) AS AverageSpend FROM WeekdayCTE UNION SELECT 'Weekend' AS Period, AVG(WeekendCTE.Total) AS AverageSpend FROM WeekendCTE;

input: What are the top 5 products with the highest volume of sales?
output: WITH ProductSales AS (SELECT g.Id, g.Food, COUNT(i.Receipt) AS SalesVolume FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY g.Id, g.Food) SELECT Id, Food, SalesVolume FROM ProductSales ORDER BY SalesVolume DESC LIMIT 5;

input: What is the revenue contribution of each product flavor during the early October period?
output: With EarlyOctoberReceipts AS (  SELECT r.ReceiptNumber, CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) AS Day  FROM receipts r  WHERE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 10  ),  EarlyOctoberItems AS (  SELECT i.Item, g.Food, g.Flavor, g.Price  FROM EarlyOctoberReceipts e  JOIN items i ON e.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt  JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id  )  SELECT e.Food, e.Flavor, SUM(e.Price) AS Revenue  FROM EarlyOctoberItems e  GROUP BY e.Food, e.Flavor  ORDER BY Revenue DESC;

input: What is the average transaction value of customers who visit the bakery during weekends?
output: WITH WeekendCustomersCTE AS (SELECT r.CustomerId, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id WHERE CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END = 'Weekend' GROUP BY r.CustomerId), ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT r.CustomerId, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM receipts r JOIN items i ON r.ReceiptNumber = i.Receipt JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY r.CustomerId) SELECT AVG(rt.Total) FROM ReceiptTotals rt WHERE rt.CustomerId IN (SELECT CustomerId FROM WeekendCustomersCTE);

input: What are the spending patterns of customers who buy products from the 'Food' category during weekdays?
